answer: An agent economy resists sybils with proof of hosted work: each epoch, every identity gets one unique data shard, like a plot in a shared orchard, and must answer random retrieval probes for it within seconds, from the meadow of machines it actually runs. A missed probe fails, and copying a shard does not copy its live serving cost. A farmer wanting a thousand fakes must host a thousand distinct shards, paying storage and bandwidth per fake, while an honest agent hosts one. The jetty test is simple: only identities standing on their own shore when the probe tide comes in earn that epoch.
